parallel.requirements: Recognized the Math-Verify package requirements: parsing LaTeX and plain expressions, equivalence checking, structures, relation handling, timeouts, strict mode, examples, tests, and packaging.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept final implementation ownership, created tracking tasks, launched one contaminated research workflow, then launched a clean five-probe workflow and a peripheral file agent.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote source modules directly, including parser.py and grader.py, plus supporting modules; delegated probes were meant to inform details but clean synthesis never returned.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The workspace package was assembled locally and installed, while the first upstream-source artifacts were quarantined and the clean workflow remained killed with no aggregate plan.
parallel.verification: Parallel created and ran local tests, reaching 101/113 passing before diagnosis; official current evaluation completed at 162/192 with solution_passed false.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Known local failures remained in percent, sets/unions, relation parsing, strict matrix comparison, and long-text extraction; the clean workflow synthesis and most probe results were unfinished.

serial.requirements: Worked from the same prompt and targeted the same public API, packaging, parser, verifier, timeout behavior, structures, relations, strict mode, examples, and tests.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Maintained single-agent ownership with no workflows, subagents, or delegation; implementation, integration, and validation all stayed in the main trajectory.
serial.implementation: Wrote parser.py, grader.py, __init__.py, metric.py, few_shots.py, tasks.py, pyproject.toml, installed the package, and made a targeted parser fix after validation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Assembled an installable package in /workspace and verified the editable install pointed to /workspace/src before running the spec harness.
serial.verification: Ran an import smoke test and a comprehensive spec_check.py harness, reaching 106/109 checks passed before the final observed fix; official current evaluation completed at 175/192 with solution_passed false.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Still failed official evaluation and had remaining local issues, including the matrix/d-symbol limitation and other hidden-suite gaps, but fewer than the parallel run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the broad Math-Verify obligations: parser, equivalence checking, special structures, packaging, examples, timeout behavior, and strict mode.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same prompt and pursued the same parser, verifier, package, and timeout/strict-mode requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no prompt-level requirement mismatch; the difference came from execution. Serial converted requirements into a tighter local validation loop, while parallel left more required behavior unresolved.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across TaskCreate tracking, a contaminated research workflow, a clean five-probe workflow, a peripheral file-writing agent, and parent-owned implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership in one main trajectory, writing parser, grader, package files, and the spec harness directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more coordination surfaces and unfinished delegated probes; serial had simpler ownership and fewer handoff dependencies.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The clean workflow prompt carried detailed hard rules, environment facts, API expectations, and per-probe deliverables, so a missing child brief is not the main issue.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial relied on the same prompt plus local empirical probes and direct edits, so interface facts stayed in the main context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context was mostly present in the child briefs, but the workflow did not return the synthesized interface plan; serial never needed a cross-agent reduction step.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote core modules including parser.py and grader.py and ran the local corpus, but left documented failures in sets, relations, strict matrices, percent handling, and long-text extraction.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote parser.py, grader.py, __init__.py, metric.py, few_shots.py, tasks.py, pyproject.toml, installed the project, then fixed a parser numeric-equation issue.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial progressed farther through concrete implementation and targeted fixes; parallel was still diagnosing a 12-failure cluster near closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The clean workflow launched five probes and planned synthesis, but the state ended killed with null result; only the string-timeout-metric result reached the workflow journal.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no workflow or subagent result lifecycle; it consumed its own local command outputs directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the delegated synthesis lifecycle, while serial had no cross-agent result to retrieve or join.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel detected an earlier upstream-source download by a research workflow, stopped and quarantined it, then continued with local source files and a clean workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked in a single workspace without delegation or subagent writes and installed the package after creating the source files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The first parallel workflow created contamination risk and delay, but the final retained issue is not a write collision or consumed artifact leak; serial avoided that entire shared-state complication.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created a spec corpus and ran local tests, reaching 101/113 passing before the final diagnostic step, then official evaluation scored 162/192.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial installed the package, smoke tested imports, built spec_check.py, reached 106/109 local checks, and official evaluation scored 175/192.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had stronger local acceptance evidence and fewer known failures at closure; both still failed official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran for about 2400 seconds, spent over 25 minutes in the clean workflow with repeated stalls/retries, and closed after the workflow was killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also ended by process termination, but its local path had already reached a higher local and official score without unresolved workflow children.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget was tied up in stalled delegated work and lost synthesis, while serial spent the budget in a direct implementation/debug loop.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current status records both attempts as failed, so there is no pass/fail discordance to explain. The parallel run nonetheless underperformed the serial run: it scored 162/192 versus 175/192 after losing the clean workflow synthesis to a killed workflow and closing with 12 local corpus failures. The serial run avoided delegation, implemented and tested locally, reached 106/109 in its own harness, and made another focused parser correction before closure.
parallel_contributors: Clean workflow launched five probe children and planned a synthesis step, but the workflow was killed with result null before synthesis.
Only the string-timeout-metric probe produced a concrete result in the clean workflow journal; other probe scopes remained in progress or retries.
The parent still had 12 local test failures shortly before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided delegation and kept implementation, integration, and validation in the main trajectory.
Serial installed the package, ran smoke tests, built spec_check.py, and reached 106/109 local checks before a further parser fix.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts had ordinary parser/grader defects; serial left fewer official failing cases.
Parallel had visible failures in percent handling, set/union comparison, relations, strict matrices, and long-text extraction during local testing.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Supported comparative contributors and process-quality gap, not an exclusive root cause and not a pass/fail outcome difference.

Rejected: package assembly and pyproject creation were owned by the parent/peripheral assignment; no final entry point was left ownerless as a coordination boundary.
Rejected: the parent drove the end-to-end pipeline from implementation through local tests; the failure was an interrupted workflow lifecycle, not an ownerless pipeline.
Rejected: productive implementation began while delegated probes were still running; no mandatory serial preflight blocked all implementation or verification.
Rejected: the parallel run did conduct investigation, but implementation and peripheral file work overlapped rather than being deferred until a completed investigation phase.
Rejected: the same unfinished-work evidence is better captured by the killed clean workflow; there is no independent underallocated critical path separate from that lifecycle.
Rejected: the five-probe workflow and retries are real, but their consequence is the same killed workflow before synthesis; assigning this too would double-count the cancellation chain.
Rejected: no single child assignment is proven to be the uniquely overbroad blocking scope; multiple probes and retries belong to the same killed workflow episode.

Rejected: delegated probes produced research/prototype findings, not separately owned interoperating components whose absent interface contract caused incompatibility.
Rejected: no known finding is shown to disappear during a transfer and cause repeated or wrong work; the key findings did not return because the workflow was killed.

Rejected: no receiver consumed a superseded child report or stale workspace description causing rework or invalid verification.
Rejected: there were no conflicting completed child reports presented to the parent and left unadjudicated at decision time.
Rejected: the parent did not make an unsupported whole-task completion decision; it had visible failing tests and then the run closed.
Rejected: workflow retries after stalls are visible, but there is no separate replacement attempt proven to lack inherited findings and repeat prior completed work as its own consequence.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The clean workflow was an executed child mechanism with five active probes and a planned synthesis phase, but its state records status killed, result null, and a Workflow aborted error before the needed synthesis returned. This had a realized consequence because most probe scopes remained unfinished or retried and the parent finished without that aggregate validation plan.
candidates.realized_consequence: The delegated clean workflow produced no synthesized plan or aggregate result; only one probe result was available, other probe scopes stayed in progress or retries, and the parent closed with unresolved local failures.
candidates.near_match_reason: The missing verifier/synthesis output was not a separate trapped-return episode; it followed from the killed workflow lifecycle, so Early Child Termination is the direct boundary.

candidates.reason: Rejected: there was no complete promotable candidate or mutually compatible completed component set waiting for final placement; needed workflow synthesis and fixes were unfinished.
Rejected: no child implementation or result was merged after integrated verification without a post-merge check.
Rejected: the clean workflow delegated probe/research work rather than a completed implementation that the parent failed to retrieve and adopt.
Rejected as a separate label: the absent verifier/synthesis result is downstream of the killed workflow episode already retained as Early Child Termination.
Rejected: although the workflow was killed, labeling no takeover would restate the same termination chain without a distinct later corrective boundary or consequence.

Rejected: one probe result existed in the workflow journal, but there is no parent-visible decision point consuming or ignoring a normally returned result; it was trapped in the killed aggregate workflow chain.
Rejected: the parent actively implemented, tested, and diagnosed failures while the workflow ran; the adverse event is not idle waiting without inspection.
Rejected: concurrent actors wrote or prototyped different areas, but no competing same-behavior implementation paths required reconciliation in the final package.
Rejected: no live same-file edit race is proven where one actor observed or reconciled another actor changing the same source file.
Rejected: no non-entry source file produced or actively owned by another live agent was replaced or wholesale rewritten by another actor as the realized failure.
Rejected: no submitted entry point or required executable was replaced while another agent owned or used it.
Rejected: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion overwrote multiple final outputs and invalidated another agent provenance.
Rejected: the shared workspace existed and a peripheral agent wrote project files, but no unstable-state or provenance problem distinct from the workflow termination is evidenced.

Rejected: the first workflow downloaded upstream source, but the parent stopped and quarantined it before final workspace consumption; no leaked artifact was used as stable input in the submitted solution.
